3B.02.t: Lateral Approaches I — Kocher & Modified Kocher
3B.02.b:
### Kocher (ECU–anconeus)
- Uses → radial head, capitellum, **LCL (lateral collateral ligament) repair**
  [[FIG: Fig 3B.3, 3B.4, 3B.5, 3B.6 · 3B.02
- Position → supine, arm across the chest, **forearm pronated** · Incision → lateral epicondyle → posterior ulnar border 6–8 cm below the olecranon tip
- Plane → **anconeus (radial) / ECU (extensor carpi ulnaris; PIN)** → the only true internervous lateral plane

1) Find the gap **distally**, where fibres diverge
2) Supinator + capsule → capsulotomy at the **equator of the radial head** → front **PIN**, back **LUCL** (lateral ulnar collateral ligament)
3) Annular ligament → open **1 cm in front of the ulna** to spare the LUCL
4) **LUCL repair** → anchor at the **most proximal point** of the epicondyle footprint, **with the extensor mass**

- Danger → **PIN** crosses the neck 2–4 cm below the head → **full pronation**; nothing below the annular ligament; no Hohmann in front of the neck
- Danger → **LUCL** just behind the interval → cut and missed → **iatrogenic PLRI** (posterolateral rotatory instability)

PITFALL — how far does pronation move the PIN?
- Prof Mansour → ≈30 mm (L03) · head-to-PIN 4 cm pronated, 2 cm supinated (L06)
- Say → "**pronation moves the PIN 1.5–3 cm away**; inside the joint supination gives more room" (Arrigoni 2019)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "approach to the radial head"
- **Kocher** → anconeus (radial) / ECU (PIN), forearm **pronated**
- Capsule at the **equator** → front = PIN, back = LUCL
- Stay **above the annular ligament**; no retractor round the neck (PIN on bone in ≈25%, Hopp)
- LCL torn (fracture-dislocation) → Kocher reaches it; LCL intact → Kaplan or EDC split spares it
- Close → repair LUCL to its isometric point (Campbell)

3B.05.t: Posterior Deep Options — Split, Sparing, Osteotomy
3B.05.b:
### Triceps split & triceps reflection
[[FIG: Fig 3B.15, 3B.16, 3B.17, 3B.18 · 3B.05
| Approach | How | Use / limit |
|---|---|---|
| **Triceps split** (Campbell) | Midline split from the tip | Extensile; open fractures; limited joint view |
| **Bryan-Morrey** | Triceps + ulnar periosteum + anconeus peeled **medial → lateral** | Arthroplasty; **triceps insufficiency** risk |
| **Paratricipital** (Alonso-Llames) | Medial (ulnar nerve) + lateral (off lateral IMS) windows; insertion intact | Extra-articular and simple intra-articular; poor for coronal shear |

- Triceps-sparing → may cut the MCL **posterior** band, never the anterior band; laterally never the LUCL

### Olecranon osteotomy
[[FIG: Fig 3B.21, 3B.22, 3B.23, 3B.24 · 3B.05
1) Find the **bare area** → dissector through the joint or K-wire under fluoroscopy
2) **Chevron, apex distal**, ≈60°
3) Saw **¾ depth** → crack the rest with an osteotome → jigsaw fit
4) **Pre-drill** the fixation before cutting

- Step-cut osteotomy → **do not do it**

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "posterior approaches to the distal humerus"
- All share **one midline incision**, full-thickness flaps, **ulnar nerve first**
- They differ by the triceps → **split** (Campbell), **reflected** (Bryan-Morrey, tongue), **spared** (paratricipital, triceps-on), **off with bone** (olecranon osteotomy)
- Most exposure → osteotomy; least triceps damage → paratricipital
- Osteotomy → chevron, apex distal, at the bare area, pre-drilled
- Arthroplasty → triceps-on or Bryan-Morrey; never osteotomy (needs the ulna)

### Henry approach to the cubital fossa
